title: Metabolic Profile of Plant Tissues by GC/MS
author: Nívea . Vieira
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8suhwew
materials: 1) Dissolve each dried aliquote with 40 µl methoxyamine hydrochloride (20 mg/ml in pyridin) and vortex for 30 seconds. Derivatize also one empty microtube as a ‘blank’. 2) Shake in thermomixer for 2 hours at 37ºC, 1000 rpm and then centrifuge fastly (“spin”) to remove the drops of cover. 3) Add 70µl MSTFA containing retention time standard (Fatty Acid Methyl Esters, FAME) (20µl/ml) and shake in thermomixer for 30 minutes at 37ºC. 4) Centrifuge fastly (“spin”) to remove the drops of cover and transfer the sample into vials.

steps.title: Sample Collection and Preparation
steps.instruction: Collect plant tissue samples and prepare them for extraction while maintaining cryogenic conditions.

substeps.instruction: Immediately freeze samples in liquid nitrogen and store at -80°C.
Macerate samples in liquid nitrogen using a mortar and pestle, ensuring they do not thaw.
Weigh approximately 100mg of each sample into high-quality 2ml microtubes and record the weight for normalization.

steps.title: Metabolite Extraction
steps.instruction: Extract polar metabolites using a methanol-chloroform-water partitioning method.

substeps.instruction: Add 700 µl of methanol and vortex for 10 seconds to stop enzymatic activity.
Add 30 µl of ribitol (from a 0.2 mg/ml water stock solution) as an internal quantitative standard for the polar phase and vortex for 10 seconds.
Shake in a termomixer for 15 minutes at 70ºC and 1000 rpm; open microtubes after 2 minutes of incubation to relieve internal pressure.
Centrifuge for 10 min at 14000 rpm and transfer the supernatant to new microtubes.
Add 375µl of chloroform and 750µl ultrapure water, vortex for 15 seconds, and centrifuge at 4000rpm for 15 minutes.
Collect the upper polar phase into new 2ml microtubes.

steps.title: Aliquoting and Drying
steps.instruction: Determine the optimal volume for derivatization and dry the samples.

substeps.instruction: Test 3 aliquots (50, 100, and 150 μl) from two contrasting samples via GC/MS to define the best volume for the remaining samples.
Dry the selected aliquots in a vacuum centrifugation drier (speedvac) overnight without heating.

steps.title: GC/MS Analysis
steps.instruction: Perform gas chromatography-mass spectrometry using a 30m capillary column.

substeps.instruction: Inject 1µl of sample in splitless mode at 230 °C with a helium flow of 2 mL/min.
Set oven temperature to 80°C initially, then increase by 15°C per minute until 330°C is reached; hold at 330°C for 5 minutes.
Acquire mass spectra using the full-scan method from 33 to 600 m/z.
Use n-alkanes series as a retention time standard to calculate the retention index.

steps.title: Data Pre-processing and TargetSearch Analysis
steps.instruction: Process raw spectra and identify metabolites using the TargetSearch R package.

substeps.instruction: Install R (32 or 64 bit) and OpenOffice.
Export raw spectra from ChromaTof (Leco TruTof) as .cdf files into a work directory (e.g., C:/myworkdirectory/).

Download and unpack 'my.work.directory.rar' into the work directory to obtain 'MainScrip.r', the GMD library ('GMDB_FAMELib_TS_20110228_IS.txt'), and correction files ('FAME_limist.txt' and 'rimLimits.txt').
Edit 'FAME_limist.txt' and 'rimLimits.txt' with lower and upper TIC limits for each alkane obtained from ChromaTof.
Open 'MainScript.r' in RStudio and edit the setwd() line to match the local working directory path.
Run lines 9-11 of the script to install the TargetSearch package.
Run lines 14-102 to load TargetSearch and execute the identification script using parameters: mass range 85-500 Da, threshold 50, TopMasses 10, r thresh 0.05, and quality index threshold 600.
Run lines 107-108 to install/load 'dplyr' and edit lines 110-111 with the correct 'profile' and 'quantmatrix' filenames to export data.

steps.title: Statistical Analysis via MetaboAnalyst
steps.instruction: Perform data normalization and statistical profiling using the MetaboAnalyst platform.

substeps.instruction: Upload the exported .txt file to MetaboAnalyst (Statistical Analysis > Peak Intensity Table, format: sample in columns unpaired).
If 'Duplicate feature names' errors occur, use OpenOffice (Ctrl+F) to rename duplicates (e.g., rename 'Abscisic acid (1MEOX) (1TMS)' to 'Abscisic acid_2 (1MEOX) (1TMS)').
Perform sample-specific normalization using fresh tissue mass: identify the sample with the highest weight as 1.0 and generate relative factors for others.
Perform internal control normalization using 'Normalization by reference feature' and selecting Ribitol, or use media/median normalization.
Apply data transformation and scaling if parametric statistics requirements (normality, homogeneity of variance) are not met.
Conduct Cluster Analysis (PCA or PSDLA) to identify treatment effects and ANOVA to detect significantly varying compounds.
Perform Pathway Analysis by altering compound synonyms in the list to match KEGG or PubChem libraries.
